Life before cars

How did people travel 150 years ago? Read aloud.

Horses and carriages

People rode horses or travelled in a carriage. A horse walks at about 6 km per hour.

Bicycles

In the 1870s people rode the penny-farthing. Its front wheel was very, very big!

Trains

The first public steam railway opened in England in 1825. Trains were fast, but they only went on rails.

A journey of 100 km took…

Horse and carriagemost of a day
Modern carabout 1 hour

Problems: muddy roads, tired horses — and city streets full of horse poo!

Karl Benz builds the first car

Germany, 1885–1886

Karl Benz was a German engineer. In 1885 he built a small car with an engine. In January 1886 he got a patent for it. A patent is an official paper that says: "This is my invention."

His car was called the Benz Patent-Motorwagen. It had three wheels, two seats and no roof.

3wheels1cylinder0.75horsepower16km/h top speed

How did the engine work?

Tap the four steps.

An engine makes a car move. It uses fuel to create power. The first cars had very small and simple engines.

The piston turns a shaft. A belt and chains turn the back wheels.

Explain it to your teacher: First… Then… After that… Finally…

Bertha Benz's big trip

August 1888 — the first long journey by car

Bertha was Karl Benz's wife. One morning in 1888 she took the car with her two teenage sons. She did not tell Karl! She drove from Mannheim to Pforzheim — about 106 km.

There were no petrol stations, so she bought fuel at a pharmacy. When a fuel pipe was blocked, she cleaned it with her hairpin. She could repair the car herself!

Henry Ford and the Model T

USA, 1903–1927

Henry Ford was an American engineer and businessman. In 1903 he started the Ford Motor Company in Detroit.

In 1908 he made the Model T. It was simple, strong and easy to repair. Ford wanted ordinary families to buy cars — not only rich people.

1908first Model T15 millionbuilt by 1927"Tin Lizzie"its nickname

The moving assembly line

Build a Model T! Tap "Next station".

Time to build one Model T
12½ hours→1½ hours
Before and after the moving assembly line (1913)

Did Henry Ford invent the assembly line?

No! Other factories used lines before him. Ford made the moving assembly line famous and used it for mass production — millions of cars.

Modern car technology

Tap a card to flip it. Then explain it in your own words.

How does an electric car work?

They use electricity stored in a battery. An electric motor turns the wheels. They do not need petrol.

Tesla (USA, 2003) made electric cars popular. The Tesla Model S (2012) could go more than 400 km on one charge.
